papers.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
papers.summary: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(μ)$ associated to a partition $μ=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for signatures \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

papers.title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
papers.summary: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. As an application of this geometrization, we prove Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets over p-adic fields: for quasisplit classical groups and their pure inner forms, all local Arthur packets are ABV-packets, and the distributions attached to these ABV-packets of Arthur type satisfy Arthur's local conjectures on twisted endoscopic character relations. This demonstrates the following general principle: for any reductive group G over a local field, an Arthur packet should be defined as an ABV-packet of Arthur type, equipped with the endoscopic pairing calculated by traces of actions on vanishing cycles or microlocalizations.

papers.summary: The Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. papers.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
papers.summary: We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure. We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture. First, the set of complex dimensions $n$ for which $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure has natural density one. Second, we explicitly identify $266$ congruence classes modulo $288$ such that $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure whenever $n>3$ lies in one of these classes. These classes cover more than $92\%$ of complex dimensions, improving the previously known lower bound of approximately $36\%$. We prove these results by first relating the concordance group of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ to suitable Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration subgroups of its stable cohomotopy group, and then applying computations in chromatic homotopy theory at height $2$.

papers.title: Higher zeroes in pointed infinity-categories
papers.summary: We construct an endofunctor on (small) simplicial sets which freely adjoins a zero object to a (small) infinity-category, as the co-cone construction freely adjoins a terminal object. We then prove that this endofunctor induces a left adjoint to the inclusion of the infinity-category of (small) pointed infinity-categories and morphisms that preserve zero objects into the infinity-category of (small) infinity-categories. This adjunction, in turn, leads to the definition of a coherent choice of nullhomotopies on a pointed infinity-category. A coherent choice of nullhomotopies is a non-canonical, coherent choice of "higher zeroes" on a pointed infinity-category, mirroring the obvious definition of higher zeroes on the differential graded nerve of a differential graded category of chain complexes over an additive category. We then show that coherent choices of nullhomotopies give an alternate characterization of fiber sequences in pointed infinity-categories, generalizing the 1-categorical definition of kernels in terms of morphisms that compose to zero.

papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.summary: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $φ^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

papers.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
papers.summary: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud cœur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion of the geometric Néron--Severi group and the local-local and local-étale parts of the finite Picard quotient.

papers.title: Toward Quillen stratification for the odd primary Steenrod algebra
papers.summary: Fix an odd prime $p$ and let $A$ be the mod $p$ Steenrod algebra. There is a normal sub-Hopf algebra $D$ of $A$, and we show that the cohomology of $A$ is $F$-isomorphic to the subalgebra of the cohomology of $D$ which is invariant under the $A$-action. We also show that the sub-Hopf algebras of $A$ with bounded profile function detect nilpotence in cohomology.

papers.title: Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations
papers.summary: We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.

papers.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
papers.summary: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: A rank-zero $2$-converse to the Gross--Zagier and Kolyvagin theorem for elliptic curves with abelian two-division field
papers.summary: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with abelian two-division field. We prove that finiteness of ${\mathrm Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ implies $L(E,1)\ne0$. The proof follows the quadratic twist deformation approach of OpenAI: Beilinson--Kato elements are interpolated over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension and over families of quadratic twists, and congruences in the resulting group ring transfer non-vanishing from the twists to $E$. The integral control of this interpolation is governed by one cohomological $μ$-invariant, which depends only on $E[2]$ and vanishes for abelian two-division fields. Together with Kato's cyclotomic divisibility and the fixed lattice in his construction, it bounds the denominator by a fixed power of $2$, independently of the twisting primes and the family dimension. Congruences among coefficients of a half-integral-weight form, in the style of Ono--Skinner, construct the required twist families.

papers.title: Indecomposable Uniform Families on the Adams 4-Line
papers.summary: We show that the $f_j$, $p_j$, $D_3(j)$, and $p_j'$ families on the 4-line of the classical Adams spectral sequence all conform to the Uniform Doomsday Conjecture. We do so by first using Bruner's formula to establish uniform families of differentials on these classes. We then study the Burklund-Xu and Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences to ensure that the differential targets are nonzero. The $f_j$ family requires further analysis of possible Adams $d_2$ differentials since the $f_j$ support uniform $d_3$ differentials. As a result of our work, only two indecomposable $\text{Sq}^0$ families remain to be settled in Adams filtration 4.

papers.title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
papers.summary: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperkähler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperkähler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperkähler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.

papers.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
papers.summary: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $χ$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $χ$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

papers.title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.

papers.title: Hessenberg character
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.

papers.title: Adelic Galois representations are maximal for almost all Drinfeld modules
papers.summary: Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, let $q$ be an odd prime power, and set $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $F=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$. We study the Galois representations associated with rank $r$ Drinfeld modules of the form $φ_T=T+g_1τ+\cdots+g_rτ^r$, where $g_i\in A$ and $g_r\neq 0$. Ordering the coefficient tuples $\vec{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ by their maximum degree, we prove that, for a density-one set of tuples, the $λ$-adic Galois representation is surjective for every prime $λ$ of $A$, and the adelic Galois image contains $\mathrm{SL}_r(\widehat A)$. Moreover, for every tuple in this set, the index of the adelic image equals the index of the corresponding rank-one determinant representation and hence divides $q-1$. These results extend Zywina's theorem in rank $2$ to arbitrary ranks $r\geq 3$. As a further consequence, we establish the existence of rank $r$ Drinfeld modules with surjective adelic Galois representations for every $r\geq 3$, extending previous existence results which were known for prime values of $r$.

papers.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
papers.summary: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.

papers.title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
papers.summary: By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems. We also examine low-dimensional representatives, including $K_1$, Steinberg-group presentations of $K_2$, and fillings related to the Steinberg relation, providing a more explicit construction of Ghys' manifold.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $Φ(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).

papers.title: On the Iwasawa invariants of admissible quadratic twists of elliptic curves at ordinary Eisenstein primes
papers.summary: We study the Iwasawa $μ$- and $λ$-invariants of quadratic twists of rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes $p\geq 3$. We verify Greenberg's $μ=0$ conjecture for all such twists, which gives an Euler system free proof of Mazur's cotorsion conjecture, and study the $λ$-invariants when the twist is admissible in the sense of [GV00]. As a consequence, we prove the cyclotomic Iwasawa Main Conjecture and obtain the $p$-part BSD formulae in rank $0$ for admissible twists under mild conditions, covering many elliptic curves of potentially ordinary reduction.

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.summary: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.summary: We study the Seshadri function on the ample cone of a smooth complex projective surface at a fixed point. At a submaximal class, we show that the function is differentiable if and only if there is a unique Seshadri curve. papers.title: The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky
papers.summary: We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties. papers.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
papers.summary: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(μ)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(μ)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

papers.title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
papers.summary: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.

papers.title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
papers.summary: Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $Λ$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. papers.title: Cohomology of regular spherical actions
papers.summary: We study regular spherical actions, namely, actions of a connected compact Lie group G on a manifold M with equidimensional orbits, some of which are spheres. These spherical orbits are diffeomorphic to homogeneous spaces G/H, and there is a list of nine possible families of pairs (G, H). The goal of this paper is to relate the cohomology of M to that of the orbit space M/G. We obtain a particularly simple relationship in the first case, W = Z_2. For the remaining two cases, W = S^1 and W = S^3, it is already known that the cohomology of M and that of the orbit space M/G are related by the Gysin sequence ... \to H^k(M/G) \to H^k(M ) \to H^{k-d}(M/G) \to H^{k+1}(M/G) \to ... In this work, we provide a direct construction of this sequence, avoiding the use of spectral sequences. Moreover, we give an explicit description of the connecting homomorphism as multiplication by a power of the Euler class associated with the action of the Weyl group W = S^l on the fixed-point set M^H.

papers.title: Magnitude, path and coarse homology
papers.summary: In this article, we introduce Borel--Moore and uniformly finite versions of magnitude homology and path homology for locally finite graphs by allowing possibly infinite chains subject to local finiteness and boundedness conditions. In both settings, we construct magnitude--path spectral sequences extending the spectral sequence studied by the author. Their E^1-pages are given by the corresponding magnitude homologies, their E^2-pages contain the corresponding path homologies on the p-axis, and they converge to coarse homology and uniformly finite homology, respectively, in the sense of Nowak--Yu. Moreover, the E^{r+1}-page is invariant under r- homotopy, whereas the homology to which the spectral sequence converges is invariant under coarse equivalence. Thus the spectral sequences interpolate between small-scale and large-scale geometry. We also show that the Borel--Moore and uniformly finite magnitude homologies are products and restricted products, respectively, of ordinary magnitude homology groups with a fixed initial point. Hence the E^1-page is assembled from pointwise magnitude-homological data, providing a mechanism for combining local information into global large-scale invariants. As applications, we establish Mayer--Vietoris sequences for magnitude homology, path homology, the associated spectral-sequence pages, and coarse and uniformly finite homology. We also show that diagonality of ordinary magnitude homology implies degeneration at the E^2-page, yielding isomorphisms between path homology and the corresponding coarse homology. Finally, we discuss applications to Cayley graphs of graph products, including right-angled Artin groups and right-angled Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Efficient congruencing in $\mathbb Z[t]$ modulo $t^2$
papers.summary: We develop an analogue of nested efficient congruencing applicable in the ring $\mathbb Z[t]/t^2\mathbb Z[t]$ so as to estimate mean values related to that of Vinogradov. Let $k$ be a natural number, and suppose that $\varphi_j(u)\in \mathbb Z[t,u]$ $(1\le j\le k)$ is a system of polynomials having Wronskian $W(u;\boldsymbol \varphi)=\det ({\rm d}^i\varphi_j(u)/{\rm d}u^i)_{1\le i,j\le k}$ with respect to $u$. Consider the number $Υ_{s,k}(X;\boldsymbol \varphi)$ of integral solutions of the system of equations \[ \sum_{i=1}^s \bigl( \varphi_j(u_i+v_it)-\varphi_j(u_{s+i}+v_{s+i}t)\bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod{t^2}\quad (1\le j\le k), \] with $|u_i|\le X$ and $|v_i|\le X$ $(1\le i\le s)$. We show that when $W(u;\boldsymbol \varphi)\not\equiv 0\pmod{t}$ and $1\le s\le k(k+1)/2$, then $Υ_{s,k}(X;\boldsymbol \varphi)\ll X^{2s+\varepsilon}$. Our conclusions extend to number fields and function fields, as we outline. We describe several consequences of our results, including forthcoming work establishing the main conjecture for certain systems of equations not possessing translation-dilation invariant properties.

papers.title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
papers.summary: We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. For an odd prime power $q$, consider polynomials over $\mathbb F_{q^n}$ of the form $\sum_{0\le i\le j<n}a_{ij}x^{q^i+q^j}+L(x)$, where $a_{ij}\in\mathbb F_{q^n}$ and $L$ serves as an $\mathbb F_q$-linear endomorphism of $\mathbb F_{q^n}$. In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not $2$, and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.

papers.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
papers.summary: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.

papers.title: Categorical Torelli and Fourier-Mukai partners of hypersurfaces
papers.summary: Let $X\subset\PP^{M-1}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$, and let $\Ku(X)$ be its Kuznetsov component, the orthogonal complement of the line bundles $\OO_X,\dots,\OO_X(M-d-1)$ in the derived category. We prove that $\Ku(X)$ determines $X$ for every smooth quartic in $\PP^{4k+1}$, $k\geq1$; together with earlier work, this gives categorical Torelli for every smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$ with $d\nmid M$. The same algebraic reconstruction proves the classical generic Torelli theorem for these quartics, which completes generic Torelli for smooth hypersurfaces whose degree does not divide $M$, cubic surfaces excepted. When $d$ divides $M$, the Kuznetsov component is a Calabi--Yau category, as for cubic fourfolds, where categorical Torelli is known to fail. We show that, apart from cubic fourfolds, such a hypersurface has a number of Fourier--Mukai partners bounded by a constant depending only on $d$ and $M$, and that categorical Torelli holds in sufficiently large degree, in every dimension. The main tool is a deformation theorem: when geometric deformations surject onto the second Hochschild cohomology of the Kuznetsov components, an equivalence deforms together with the hypersurfaces, so statements proved for general hypersurfaces extend to all smooth ones.

papers.title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
papers.summary: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I. Gringlaz, R. Kumar, B. Weiss. We also find the possible densities of the set of visible points in the cut-and-project set, with a constant generic lattice, and a changing window with constant volume. We also study bounds for the distance of large holes in the set of visible points of certain cut-and-project sets, generalizing theorems originally proved by P. Erdős for $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

papers.title: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.summary: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

papers.title: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
papers.summary: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal. For the dimension-three codes $C_L(D,(r+1)Q)$ on Hermitian curves over $\F_{r^2}$, $r=2^e\ge4$, we obtain \[ n+2g-r-2\leτ_D(C;Q)\le n+2g-3. \] Consequently the leading genus contribution is asymptotically sharp even in dimension three. On the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3$ over $\F_4$, we prove the exact dimension-three threshold $6$ by an explicit multiplier. For repetition codes on the Hermitian family, the threshold equals the general interpolation bound $n+2g-1$. The upper bounds use information sets and hold for $q>3k$, and for $q>2k$ in characteristic two.
